title: Surjectivity and closed images for adequate moduli spaces
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\mathcal X$ be an algebraic stack over $k$, let $Y$ be an algebraic space over $k$, and let $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ be an adequate moduli space [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. Underlying spaces and 2-fibre products have the conventions of [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets]. Then $|\phi|$ is surjective. For every morphism of algebraic spaces $T\to Y$, the continuous map $|\mathcal X\times_YT|\to|T|$ is closed. For any two closed substacks $\mathcal Z_1,\mathcal Z_2\subseteq\mathcal X$, one has the equality of subsets of $|Y|$
$$\phi(|\mathcal Z_1|)\cap\phi(|\mathcal Z_2|)=\phi(|\mathcal Z_1\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z_2|).$$
No finite-type, reducedness, characteristic-zero, or finite-inertia hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Alper, arXiv:1005.2398v3, Theorem 5.3.1(1),(2),(4), printed pp.29--30. Primary PDF read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/1005.2398; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-universal-closed-topology] for all scheme maps to $Y$. All 2-fibre products $\mathcal X_T$, $\mathcal X_W=\mathcal X_T\times_TW$ below are algebraic stacks by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products], so the topology statements of [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets] apply to them. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$. Its pullback map $|\mathcal X_V|\to|V|$ is surjective; lifting a point of $Y$ first to $V$ and then to $\mathcal X_V$ proves surjectivity of $|\phi|$. For any algebraic space $T\to Y$, choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $W\to T$. If $D\subseteq|\mathcal X_T|$ is closed, its inverse image $D_W$ is closed. The cited scheme assertion applied to $W\to Y$ makes its image in $W$ closed. Write $D=|\mathcal D|$ for the reduced closed substack given by [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets]; by its point-surjectivity clause $|\mathcal D\times_TW|$ has image $D_W$ in $|\mathcal X_W|$, and by the same lemma images commute with this base change, so that image equals the inverse image in $W$ of the image of $D$ in $T$. The topology of $T$ is the quotient topology of its atlas; hence the image of $D$ in $T$ is closed. This proves the first two clauses, without asserting that arbitrary base changes of $\phi$ remain adequate.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.1(1),(2),(4), pp.29--30; disjoint-substack power-lifting argument giving (4). Read online https://arxiv.org/pdf/1005.2398; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Set $\mathcal Z=\mathcal Z_1\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal Z_2$ and $C=\phi(|\mathcal Z|)$. It is a closed subset by Step 1. The inclusion $C\subseteq\phi(|\mathcal Z_1|)\cap\phi(|\mathcal Z_2|)$ follows from the two projections. For the reverse inclusion, fix $y\notin C$ and choose an affine etale neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ of a lift $u$ of $y$, factoring through $Y\setminus C$. Such charts are obtained by restricting an etale scheme atlas to the inverse image of this open and then taking an affine open containing a lift. By [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets], the two closed substacks $\mathcal Z_{1,U},\mathcal Z_{2,U}$ of $\mathcal X_U$ are disjoint on point spaces: a point in their intersection would lift to their 2-fibre product and hence map into $C$. Since $\mathcal X_U$ is an algebraic stack over $k$ by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products], apply [lem-sfb-disjoint-closed-substacks-algebra-quotient] on $\mathcal X_U$: its canonical map $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X_U}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal B_1\times\mathcal B_2$ is a surjection of quasi-coherent algebras.

source.place: Theorem 5.3.1(1),(2),(4), pp.29--30; disjoint-substack power-lifting argument giving (4). Read online https://arxiv.org/pdf/1005.2398; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply condition (2) of [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space] on this affine etale chart to the section $(0,1)$ of the quotient algebra from Step 2. It supplies a positive integer $N$ and $f\in\Gamma(\mathcal X_U,\mathcal O)$ mapping to $(0,1)^N=(0,1)$. Condition (1), evaluated on $U$ with the direct-image convention of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], identifies $f$ with the pullback of $a\in A$. Thus $a$ restricts to zero on $\mathcal Z_{1,U}$ and to one on $\mathcal Z_{2,U}$. If $y$ belonged to both original images, the base-change image assertion of [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets] would put $u$ in both images over $U$. Choose field-valued representatives of points over $u$ in each substack. The residue homomorphisms $\kappa(u)\to L_1,L_2$ are injective; evaluation therefore gives both $a(u)=0$ and $a(u)=1$ in the field $\kappa(u)$, a contradiction. Hence every point in both images lies in $C$, proving the equality.

Source: I downloaded Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3 and read Thm 5.3.1 on p.30. The item states exactly clauses (1) surjective, (2) universally closed (base changes by algebraic spaces) and (4) im Z1∩im Z2=im(Z1∩Z2), with no added hypotheses. Alper derives (4) from Lemma 5.2.12(2). The worker's proof of (4) takes a different route that is still valid: remove the closed image C, then on an affine étale chart over Y∖C lift (0,1) by power lifting (condition (2)) to a regular function (condition (1)), which must take the values 0 and 1 at u. Step 1 uses the existing scheme-test node lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-universal-closed-topology plus quotient topology and base change of images, which I checked against the statements. The new node lem-sfb-disjoint-closed-substacks-algebra-quotient is true: B_a is the big-site sheaf of x^*i_*O, hence quasi-coherent, and disjointness on affine T gives I1+I2=R, so CRT makes O→B1×B2 surjective. I tested it with empty Z_a, empty X, nonreduced ideals and char p. It is statement-only, self-contained, and not a clause of the item. The only near-match in the DAG is the ring-level Mathlib CRT node lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product, which is not a duplicate. No cycle. No SGA. Batch-5 flags: all four cited closures reach trf only through general definitions (def-trf-algebraic-space, def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module), outside both assumptions, so I accepted them. FIX (C1/E1): Steps 1 and 2 apply the topology lemma and the new node to X_T, X_W, X_U without showing these are algebraic stacks. I added lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products (same unit; its tool_use already recorded) to the steps and to proof_deps. Step 1 now also uses the reduced closed substack on D and its point surjectivity for the image of D_W. Only proof/proof_deps changed. lean.statement: theorem adequate_moduli_topological_images (k : Type u) [Field k] (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) (Y : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (φ : BasedFunctor F (discreteModuli Y.obj.obj)) (hφ : IsAdequateModuliSpace F hF Y φ) : Function.Surjective (moduliPointMap φ) ∧ (∀ (T : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (.of k))) (t : T ⟶ Y), @Continuous _ _ (moduliSmoothPointTopology (moduliTwoFiberProduct φ (discreteModuliMap t.hom.hom))) (moduliSmoothPointTopology (discreteModuli T.obj.obj)) (moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberSnd φ (discreteModuliMap t.hom.hom))) ∧ @IsClosedMap _ _ (moduliSmoothPointTopology (moduliTwoFiberProduct φ (discreteModuliMap t.hom.hom))) (moduliSmoothPointTopology (discreteModuli T.obj.obj)) (moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberSnd φ (discreteModuliMap t.hom.hom)))) ∧ (∀ Z₁ Z₂ : ClosedModuliSubstack F, (moduliPointMap φ '' Set.range (moduliPointMap Z₁.inclusion)) ∩ (moduliPointMap φ '' Set.range (moduliPointMap Z₂.inclusion)) = moduliPointMap φ '' Set.range (moduliPointMap ((moduliTwoFiberFst Z₁.inclusion Z₂.inclusion).comp Z₁.inclusion)))
